fatal_errors: The intervention does not identify the decisive replacement of EAM by an MTP for phase-space sampling or thermodynamic integration by free-energy perturbation.
The proposed structural mediator, local lattice distortion and dislocation motion, is unrelated to the target free-energy acceleration mechanism.
The cited evidence does not support machine-learned free-energy perturbation, computational speedup, or faithful solid-liquid free-energy calculations.
The proposed 500–2000 K boundary is unsupported and largely excludes the target 2000–2400 K regime.
The benchmark against experimental free energies is not a decisive or generally feasible validation of the computational method and omits direct FEP-versus-TI phase free-energy comparison.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad problem—reducing the cost of DFT-quality thermodynamics in multicomponent high-entropy systems—and correctly names explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD as baselines. It also identifies training-data quality and exchange-correlation choice as limitations. However, it only proposes generic machine-learning integration and misses the central methodological hypothesis: a high-fidelity MTP should sample both phases closely enough to DFT that low-variance MTP-to-DFT free-energy perturbation can replace slow thermodynamic integration. It omits the TaVCrW BCC system, 0 GPa conditions, PBE/LDA comparison, large-cell sampling, sub-meV-per-atom training and free-energy criteria, electronic excitation effects, and solid-state short-range-order stabilization. Its cost and accuracy predictions are arbitrary and do not reproduce the approximately 80% savings or 20-fold speedup and less than 0.5 meV/atom FEP–TI agreement. Evidence E1 concerns empirical potentials and structural/SRO validation, while E2 concerns experimentally observed polymorphism; neither validates ML-assisted FEP or the claimed savings. A decisive test should compare solid and liquid DFT-referenced free energies from MTP-FEP against EAM/TI or direct ab initio TI, require agreement near 0.5 meV/atom, and propagate those free energies to melting temperature, electronic-excitation shifts, and SRO contributions.
